nodes.text: Guild yard — mind the stock, the pillars bite. Petra, master mason. Every course of every terrace you climbed today was guild work, so in a manner of speaking you've been standing on my family since the gate.

First pick, my own swing. The Warden gave the order, but the guild insisted the breaking be ours — my grandfather helped SET those stones, after the trouble took the deep crews. Twenty years the guild held that seal like a held breath. Breaking your own grandfather's best work with his own initials under your pick... there's no word for that feeling. 'Family trade' is as close as I've got.

The old works, standing. Every bench where the crews left it, the stock still racked, one brazier the guild's kept fed by way of the ledge crack all these years — don't ask, guild secret, the answer's 'stubbornness'. And the market floor... swept. Twenty years sealed, and swept. Kobolds don't sweep. We put it in the report and none of us has mentioned it since, which tells you what the guild thinks of it.

The Masons raised the terraces in my great-great-grandmother's time — cut the stair, hung the arches, taught the mountain to hold a city. The guild law is one line: _stone outlasts the reasons._ Build so that when the reasons are forgotten, the work still deserves to stand. The Undercroft was our finest hour twice now — once building it, once sealing it. We'll see what the third time asks.
Mind the edge on the stair — guild-cut, but gravity's not a member.
